title: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013

divisions.question: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013 - Second Reading - Read a second time

speeches.speaker: Tony Abbott
speeches.brief: Introduced a private member's bill to raise penalties on dishonest union officials to $340,000 with up to five years' imprisonment, well above the government's recent increase to just $6,600 for individuals, citing Ian Temby QC's finding that around $20 million of Health Services Union members' money may have been misused.

speeches.speaker: Julie Bishop
speeches.brief: Moved the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013, citing Health Services Union fraud allegations of around $20 million against maximum existing penalties of $6,600 for individuals and $33,000 for organisations, proposed raising penalties to $340,000 with criminal sanctions including up to five years imprisonment, and called for a judicial inquiry into Australian Workers Union slush fund allegations from between 1992 and 1996 involving Bruce Wilson.

speeches.speaker: Michelle Rowland
speeches.brief: Opposed the Leader of the Opposition's Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013, noted a Senate committee report recommending against the bill after only two of seven submissions supported it, from the New South Wales government and the Institute of Public Affairs, cited Australian Bureau of Statistics figures showing employment rose by 71,500 in February, and highlighted an Institute of Public Affairs list of proposed cuts worth $23.5 billion.

speeches.speaker: Sussan Ley
speeches.brief: Supported the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013, contrasted the roughly $6,000 penalty for misuse of union funds with penalties above $200,000 under the Corporations Act, cited the Electrical Trades Union's purchase of a $1.25 million property in Oyster Bay for an official as an example of fund misuse, and noted the CFMEU's Victorian branch holds net assets of $42 million.

speeches.speaker: Rob Mitchell
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013, recalled that the Leader of the Opposition created the 'Australians For Honest Politics' fund in 1998 to bankroll legal action against Pauline Hanson, noted a Senate committee found only two of seven submissions supported the bill, and pointed to allegations against Moreton Bay Liberal National Party figure Scottie Driscoll as evidence the opposition ignored misconduct elsewhere.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: Supported the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013 as establishing a level playing field between unions and corporations, cited eight major Fair Work Australia investigations into alleged union misconduct and the Temby report's estimate that up to $20 million of Health Services Union funds was improperly used, and noted the bill would raise penalties from about $6,600 for individuals to $340,000 with criminal sanctions.

speeches.speaker: Mike Symon
speeches.brief: Opposed the Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Amendment (Towards Transparency) Bill 2013, argued registered organisations and corporations serve fundamentally different purposes, and cited 2,454 ASIC court proceedings against companies and their office holders over a 10 year period, including 385 criminal convictions and 212 terms of imprisonment for directors.
